Tartor
Martine Thibodeaux: Outlands and Beyond
Outlands is a series of seven oil paintings that Thibodeaux completed
Museum
at an artists colony in Taos, New Mexico. This series is part of her
forest phase, during which she concentrated on studies of woodland
plants and settings. Time, the third painting in the Outlands series,
About
was dedicated to Thibodeaux’s teacher and mentor, Henri Pochon.
The forest-phase paintings, completed over a period of twelve years,
Exhibiti
are regarded as her most accomplished works. Paintings from this
phase have been exhibited in the Gateworthy Gallery in New York
and the Prinz Ostend Gallery in Amsterdam. The Taylor Museum is
Tours
pleased to present 25 of Thibodeaux’s paintings, including Outlands
and several later works.
Events:
Shop
August | at 7:00 P.M. in the Tobin Gallery: Opening reception for
Martine Thibodeaux: Outlands and Beyond
August 5 at 6:00 P.M. in the Museum Rotunda: Presentation by art
historian Ursula Beake
Must-See Thibodeaux Exhibit
(August 7)—The Taylor Museum’s exhibition
of paintings by Martine Thibodeaux includes
the Outlands series. The exhibition runs
through the end of August and masterfully
showcases some of the artist’s most celebrated
landscape pieces. Ms. Thibodeaux planned
and sketched her Outlands series in Geneva,
Switzerland. She later completed the series
while residing in Taos, where she committed
the initial drawings done in Geneva to paint
and canvas. These details about
Ms. Thibodeaux’s work were discussed
thoroughly in an evening lecture at the
museum. This Taylor Museum exhibition is
most certainly worth a visit—Elton Liu
